definition: Human image synthesis is technology that can be applied to make believable and even photorealistic renditions of human-likenesses, moving or still.
details: It has effectively existed since the early 2000s. Many films using computer generated imagery have featured synthetic images of human-like characters digitally composited onto the real or other simulated film material. Towards the end of the 2010s deep learning artificial intelligence has been applied to synthesize media that look like humans, without need for human assistance, once the training phase has been completed, whereas the old school 7D-route required massive amounts of human work.

explainer.lead: Human image synthesis produces believable, even photorealistic, renditions of human likenesses, moving or still. It matters because it has moved from labor-intensive film compositing to deep-learning generation needing no human assistance once trained.

tiers.eli5: It makes fake pictures or videos of people that look real, and modern AI can do it without someone hand-building each one.
tiers.practitioner: The technology has effectively existed since the early 2000s, with film CGI compositing synthetic human-like characters onto real or simulated footage. Deep learning applied in the late 2010s removed the need for the massive human work of the older route, once training was complete.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as technology that can make believable and even photorealistic renditions of human likenesses, moving or still; the older approach required substantial human effort, while the deep-learning approach synthesizes such media without human assistance after training.

explainer.example: A film composites a digitally created human character onto live-action footage, a task that once required extensive manual work but can now be produced by a trained model.
